I analyse data.

units.Soy Borja Mora, <strong>Data Analyst Jun: I’m Borja Mora, a Junior Data Analyst. I’m building my career in data, with Power BI as my specialism and SQL and Python as my analysis tools. I analyse the data, understand what sits behind each result and look for the best way to visualise and communicate it.
units.Todo proyecto empieza con la misma pregu: Every project starts with the same question: what does the person looking at this need to decide? The tools come later.
I interview whoever owns the project. I work out which decision they need to make. I define the 3–5 KPIs that really matter and drop the noise. Before I open any tool, I’m clear on the question the analysis has to answer.
units.Conecto las fuentes, limpio los datos y: I connect the sources, clean the data and model the star schema. I use SQL, Python or Power Query depending on the source and the volume. I validate relationships, remove duplicates and document every transformation. If this layer fails, everything built on top of it breaks.
units.Escribo las medidas DAX que traducen pre: I write the DAX measures that turn business questions into numbers you can decide with. I cross dimensions, spot patterns and check every calculation against the data. I don’t show figures — I build answers that hold up when someone asks “why is that?”.
units.Diseño el layout antes de tocar Power BI: I design the layout before I touch Power BI — with PBI Mockup Creator, a tool I built myself. I decide what leads the view, what supports it and what goes. I use visual hierarchy, context and narrative so that whoever looks at the dashboard can make a decision without anyone having to explain it. I cover it in full in my Data Storytelling guide.
units.Seis problemas reales.<br><em>Seis respu:
Six real problems.
Six answers with data.
units.Cada uno empieza con una pregunta de neg: Each one starts with a business question and ends with something someone can use to decide.
units.Informe de ventas con enfoque IBCS: Sales report with an IBCS approach
units.En muchos equipos el análisis de ventas: In many teams, sales analysis starts and ends with the total. I built a report that applies the IBCS standard to bring volume, absolute change and percentage into a single visual, with three chart types depending on the angle you read it from.
units.En la mayoría de empresas la información: In most companies, financial information is scattered. I built a system that connects the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow into a single read, with drill-down to the journal entry behind each number.
units.Una distribuidora de hostelería, 400 cli: A hospitality distributor, 400 customers and a fall in revenue nobody could explain. The RFM analysis found €198,000 at risk in the segment that generated half of the business.
units.¿Todos tus clientes merecen la misma ofe: Do all your customers deserve the same offer?
units.Una cadena de electrónica trataba a todo: An electronics chain treated all its customers the same way: the same offers, the same emails and similar discounts. With 6,000 customers and 26 variables, it needed to find behaviour patterns that would let it personalise its campaigns.
units.Seleccioné 9 variables de comportamiento: I selected 9 behavioural variables related to spend, frequency and channel. The analysis identified 4 customer profiles, from premium to at risk of leaving, and matched a strategy to each one.
units.¿Qué pasa con las ventas cuando ocurre a: What happens to sales when something unexpected happens?
units.Una cadena retail podía prever bastante: A retail chain could forecast normal weeks fairly well, but its predictions failed when promotions, strikes or logistics problems came up. The history explained the past, but not always what was happening around it.
units.Comparé dos modelos sobre 156 semanas: u: I compared two models over 156 weeks: one based only on historical sales and another that added five external variables. I validated them with time-based backtesting and simulated more than ten future scenarios.
units.error frente al modelo basado solo en hi: error compared with the history-only model
units.¿A quién estamos a punto de perder?: Who are we about to lose?
units.Una aerolínea clasificaba a sus pasajero: An airline sorted its passengers into three tiers with rigid rules: Basic, Frequent and Premium. But those rules didn’t always reflect how people actually behaved, so it was hard to know who really needed a loyalty action.
units.Probé tres modelos sobre 21 variables de: I tested three models on 21 variables covering flights, spend and incidents, validated them against a baseline and analysed which variables helped tell the different passenger profiles apart.
units.Vista previa del dashboard Executive Ove: Preview of the Casa Origen Executive Overview dashboard in Power BI
units.Ilustración en acuarela de la fachada ro: Watercolour illustration of Casa Origen’s red shopfront in Lavapiés
units.Construí un sistema de Business Intellig: I built a complete business intelligence system to find out what was really going on behind the business: which products to drop, which bundles to create, when to stop opening and which customers to win back.
units.SQL, modelado de datos, Power BI y Machi: SQL, data modelling, Power BI and machine learning connected in a single system, to go from the business question to a concrete decision.

units.Dos periodos pueden cerrar con el mismo: Two periods can close with the same total and have been completely different underneath — without the change built into the visual, you can’t see that difference.
units.En muchos equipos comerciales el análisi: In many sales teams, sales analysis starts and ends with the total. If the figure goes up, all is well. The problem is that two periods can close with the same number and have been completely different underneath: one with real growth, the other with a fall offset by a one-off campaign. Without the change built into the visual, you can’t see that difference.
units.Construir un informe de ventas que permi: To build a sales report that lets you read volume and change in a single view, without switching tabs or comparing separate tables. And to do it following the IBCS standard, which defines how to show that information so that everyone reads it the same way, without ambiguity.
units.El estándar <strong>IBCS (International: The IBCS (International Business Communication Standards) standard sets concrete rules for showing change: which colour means a positive variance, which shape means actual versus budget, and how volume and change share the same axis without overlapping or getting mixed up.
units.Construí tres tipos de visual siguiendo: I built three types of visual following that standard. The multi-tier column chart shows the monthly absolute value, the absolute change against last year and the percentage change at the same time. The column chart with built-in change packs that information into each bar, which helps when the axis has many items. The variance line chart shows the trend over time, with the area between the actual line and the target shaded according to whether the target is met.
units.La clave técnica está en combinar <stron: The technical key is combining DAX with visual calculations: DAX for the model’s core logic and the dynamic measure selector, and visual calculations to generate the changes directly on the visual without multiplying measures in the model.
units.<strong>Power BI</strong> para el modelo: Power BI for the model, the three IBCS visual types and navigation between views. DAX and visual calculations together for the CY vs SPLY and against-target changes.
units.Replicar el estándar IBCS en Power BI si: Replicating the IBCS standard in Power BI without custom visuals forces you to understand how measure-level conditional formatting works. The hardest part was keeping the three tiers of the multi-tier column chart in the right proportions whatever the value range of the selected filter.
Free cash flow went from −€1.17m to €678,208 in one year — the model shows exactly which items explain the difference.
units.Cuando cada área analiza su parte por se: When each area analyses its own part separately, leadership has to build the full picture by hand every time. That process is slow, hard to trace and produces different versions of the same reality. Without a model that connected the three financial statements consistently, any analysis was a partial snapshot.
units.Diseñar una estructura contable que unif: To design an accounting structure that brought together the balance sheet, P&L and cash flow, stayed consistent across periods and let you navigate from a high-level KPI down to the exact journal entry behind it, without leaving the report.
units.Empecé por el modelo. <strong>Dos tablas: I started with the model. Two fact tables: FactDiario with the actual accounting entries and FactPresupuesto with the budget data, connected to the same dimensions. A TablaFechaCierre table handles the year-end projection: it extrapolates the expected year-end result from the actual data available up to the cut-off date.
units.El informe tiene seis áreas: <strong>pan: The report has six areas: a KPI panel with EBITDA, ROE, ROA, acid test, solvency and free cash flow; a validation checklist that catches unbalanced entries and unclassified accounts; a trial balance with drill-through to the individual entry; a balance sheet with vertical and horizontal analysis; a P&L with three views; and cash flow with the three types of flow compared with the previous year.
units.El checklist de validación fue una de la: The validation checklist was one of the most important decisions. In a model that consolidates several companies, a page dedicated to catching unbalanced entries and unclassified accounts stops an accounting error from reaching a board meeting as if it were a real result. In 2023, free cash flow was €678,208 against −€1,165,649 the year before.
units.<strong>Power BI</strong> para el modelo: Power BI for the full model, navigation between the six areas and drill-through to the source accounting entry. DAX for solvency and liquidity ratios, EBITDA, year-on-year change, variance against budget and the year-end projection logic.
units.Consolidar varias empresas en un único m: Consolidating several companies in a single model adds a layer of complexity that single-company projects don’t have. The year-end projection was the hardest technical piece: it has to tell months with actual data apart from months without it, and stay consistent in both the table and the trend chart.
units.Revenue en riesgo · clientes Loyal inact: Revenue at risk · inactive Loyal customers
units.111 clientes Loyal generaban casi la mit: 111 Loyal customers generated almost half the revenue and hadn’t bought anything for months — €198,000 at risk that, without segmentation, had neither a name nor a number.
units.El director comercial tenía los números: The sales director had the numbers but couldn’t make sense of them. Revenue falling, customer base growing. The first reaction was to look for more sales. But first we had to confirm whether the problem was in acquisition or retention. Without a way to see how each customer actually behaves, that question has no answer.
units.Clasificar a los 400 clientes según su c: To classify the 400 customers by how they really buy — when they last bought, how often and how much — to find which segments were losing activity and how much revenue was genuinely at risk.
units.Construí un modelo <strong>RFM</strong>: I built an RFM model on the order history. Each customer gets three scores: Recency (days since the last purchase), Frequency (number of orders) and Monetary (total amount spent). The cut-offs are calculated with dynamic percentiles across the whole table, so the model works well with any data distribution.
units.El modelo vive sobre un <strong>esquema: The model sits on a star schema with Fact_Pedidos at the centre and five dimensions: Customer, Date, Product, Sales rep and Venue type. The dashboard answers four questions on a single page: business health, split by segment, monthly revenue trend and the recommended sales action for each group — the last one generated as an HTML table straight from a DAX measure.
units.El segmento <strong>Loyal concentraba 11: The Loyal segment held 111 customers and almost half of total revenue. Their recency had been growing for months. More than €198,000 in customers who used to buy well and had not been seen for a while. Without segmentation, that signal gets lost in the total. Champions were only 34 customers, with an average recency of 14 days and an average order of €4,787, and they were treated the same as everyone else.
units.<strong>Power BI</strong> para el modelo: Power BI for the model and the full dashboard, with filters by area, venue, sales rep and year. DAX for the three scores, the segment assignment and the sales action table, generated as HTML inside a measure.
units.Lo complicado fue decidir los cortes de: The tricky part was deciding the segmentation cut-offs: when a customer moves from Loyal to At Risk can’t be an arbitrary number. Using dynamic percentiles instead of fixed thresholds was the decision that improved the model most. Generating an HTML table from DAX forces you to think harder about the design before writing the first line of code.

Mahon was the store with the highest sales (€277,000), but not the most profitable — margin by category told a story the total was hiding.
units.Una cadena de tiendas con datos completo: A store chain with complete data in its tills but no way to answer basic business questions: which store performs best, where margin is being lost, whether targets are met or it’s just beating last month. The data existed; the problem was that nobody could read it together.
units.Diseñar un <strong>sistema de reporting: To design a complete reporting system — from the data model to the dashboard — that turned scattered numbers into concrete decisions. With a single report, leadership had to be able to see sales, profitability and target attainment for each store in one read.
units.El modelo tiene <strong>dos tablas de he: The model has two fact tables: Ventas with the actual till data and Presupuestos with the targets by store and period. Both connect to the same dimensions through disconnected T_DISC tables that let you change the axis of analysis without affecting the model’s relationships. The TopN parameters filter the most relevant stores or products dynamically.
units.El informe cubre cuatro ángulos: <strong: The report covers four angles: an executive summary with sales, margin and attainment KPIs; store analysis with a ranking and comparison against target; product analysis with average order, units and profitability; and trends over time with YTD and year-on-year comparison.
units.La lectura conjunta de ventas y margen r: Reading sales and margin together revealed high-volume, low-profitability stores that weren’t visible in the previous reports. The drill-down to the individual receipt identified the exact product that explained the variance in a specific store, something that used to mean exporting to Excel and cross-referencing by hand.
units.<strong>Power BI</strong> para el modelo: Power BI for the full model and the dashboard, with navigation between the four areas. DAX for attainment against budget, YTD, year-on-year change, margin by product and dynamic ranking logic with TopN parameters. Power Query to bring together the till sources and the targets.
units.Las tablas desconectadas T_DISC son impr: Disconnected T_DISC tables are essential when the same selector has to affect two fact tables without creating ambiguity in the model. Designing the model with that separation from the start avoids having to rebuild the relationships when the business grows and adds new stores or product lines.
